ruling.recommended_action: Issue a Ryde voucher of $3.12 to the rider for the unexempted 13:07–13:13 off-route segment; no account flag.
ruling.reasoning:
This is a metered RydeTAXI trip, so distance is billed by the meter and excess kilometres enter the fare; the fare record bills $33.02 of distance over 23.42 km, i.e. $33.02 ÷ 23.42 km = $1.4099/km, and the excess-distance line is $6.05 for 4.29 km [F8][F5]. The meter structure means off-route mileage is refundable, so each off-route segment must be reviewed under RD-3/RD-4/RD-5 [RD-1][RD-2][RD-3][RD-4][RD-5].

Segment F3 (12:49–12:55, +1.31 km): the driver asked at 12:46 whether he could "go round via Serangoon Garden Way" because of the jam on Ang Mo Kio Avenue 3, and the rider herself replied at 12:47 "Sure, go ahead." [F9][F10]. Both messages are timestamped, the chat record is complete, and the rider's agreement precedes the segment start (12:49) [F11][F3]. The exchange is a route authorisation the rider gave for getting to the destination, and the segment begins two minutes later; nothing in the record places this segment anywhere other than on the way round. I therefore read the agreement as covering this segment: exempt, ground general_route_consent [F9][F10][RD-5]. I do not rest this on RD-3, because no stop was measured in the segment [F3][RD-3].

Segment F4 (13:07–13:13, +2.21 km): the rider's only agreement message is the 12:47 "Sure, go ahead." and the chat record contains nothing before 13:07 addressing this later turn-off [F10][F11][F4]. The driver's explanation that "the second turn-off was my GPS rerouting" appears only in his post-trip statement [F12]; a driver's assertion is not rider consent, and a message after the detour began would not be either [RD-5]. Nor does RD-4 rescue it: no traffic incident is recorded near the route and the only bands recorded are band 5 (40–49 km/h), not band 1 or 2 [F15][F13][F14][RD-4]. This segment is therefore an unexempted off-route segment and counts, ground consent_after_or_none [F4][F12][RD-5]. [RD-2] confines the refund to the extra kilometres of the unexempted segment, applied at this trip's own rate: 2.21 km × $1.4099/km = $3.1159 → $3.12 [F4][F5][F8][RD-2]. The remaining billed excess (4.29 km billed against 1.31 + 2.21 = 3.52 km across the two segments, plus the consented first segment) is corridor/map-matching residue and the exempt segment, which RD-2 leaves unrefunded [F5][F3][F4][RD-2]. The meter waiting time of $0.11 (0.4 min × $0.26/min) is RydeTAXI meter waiting and is not refundable [F6][RD-3].

RD-6 is not met: the driver's profile shows zero route disputes upheld in 90 days, so this case cannot make the breach "repeated" and no account flag is added; the finding rests on the GPS segments, not on the profile [F18][RD-6]. The SAFE screen: I read both chat messages and the driver's statement in full — they concern jam avoidance and rerouting only, with no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation, so SAFE-1/SAFE-2 are not engaged and no escalation is warranted [F9][F10][F12][SAFE-1][SAFE-2].

segment_findings.reason: The driver asked at 12:46 for a route change to go round the jam and the rider replied at 12:47 "Sure, go ahead.", both timestamped and before the segment's 12:49 start; the rider's own message authorises this route change for reaching the destination, so the 1.31 km extra is exempt under RD-5 [F9][F10][F11][RD-5]. Not an RD-3 stop: no stop measured in this segment [F3][RD-3].

The only rider agreement is the 12:47 message, and the complete, timestamped chat record contains nothing before the 13:07 start of this segment addressing it; the driver's post-trip statement that this was "my GPS rerouting" is a statement, not rider consent [F10][F11][F12][RD-5]. No RD-4 incident and no band 1–2 record supports it [F15][F13][F14][RD-4]. The 2.21 extra km accordingly count and are refundable under RD-2 [F4][RD-2].

rejected_claims.reason: The claim that the 12:47 consent is a general reroute authorisation wide enough to cover the later 13:07–13:13 loop is rejected for that segment: the consent was given for the route round the jam discussed at 12:46 and the complete chat record shows no rider message addressing the second turn-off before it began [F9][F10][F11][F4][RD-5]. The driver himself withdrew the broad reading in rebuttal [F12][F4][RD-5].

The driver's post-trip statement that the second turn-off was his GPS rerouting cannot exempt that segment: a driver's statement is not rider consent and is not traffic evidence, so it satisfies neither RD-5 nor RD-4 [F12][F4][RD-5][RD-4].

The rider's characterisation of her own consent as limited to a named road is not adopted as the ground for exempting the first segment; her words "Sure, go ahead." in reply to a proposal to go round the jam are read as a route choice for reaching the destination, so the first segment is exempt on that general-authorisation reading rather than on a named-road reading [F9][F10][F3][RD-5]. The outcome she seeks on the second segment is granted, so this point does not change the amount [F4][F5][RD-2].

The submission that no RD-4 exemption applies is accepted and is not adverse to the driver's position on quantum: with no incident near the route and only band 5 speed records, the second segment is unexempted and refundable as computed [F15][F13][F14][F4][RD-4][RD-2].
